title: Eventual first-jet interpolation on an ample smooth curve
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $D$ be a smooth proper integral finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $A$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_D$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let $T$ be a nonempty finite set of distinct $k$-rational closed points and $x\in T$. For $y\in T$ write $R_y=\mathcal O_{D,y}$ and $\mathfrak m_y$ for its maximal ideal; these rings are discrete valuation rings, namely local domains with nonzero principal maximal ideal in which every nonzero element is a unit times a unique nonnegative power of a generator. Let $Z\subset D$ be the finite closed subscheme with support $T$ and local rings $R_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$, and let $\mathcal I_Z$ be its ideal. There is $n_0\geq1$ such that for every $n\geq n_0$, $A^{\otimes n}$ is generated by global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], $H^1(D,\mathcal I_Z\otimes A^{\otimes n})=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology], and the restriction map $\Gamma(D,A^{\otimes n})\to\Gamma(Z,A^{\otimes n}|_Z)$ is surjective. Tensor powers use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In particular, for any choice of a frame of $A^{\otimes n}|_Z$ on each component and any generator $u$ of $\mathfrak m_x$, there exists $a\in\Gamma(D,A^{\otimes n})$ whose coefficient is $u$ modulo $\mathfrak m_x^2$ at $x$ and $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m_y^2$ for every $y\in T\setminus\{x\}$. A frame means a basis of the free rank-one module on that component. Thus $a$ has a simple zero at $x$, meaning its coefficient lies in $\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$, and is nonzero at every other point of $T$.

proof.text: A field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so $k$ is Noetherian and its one-point affine spectrum is a Noetherian scheme by the definitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $D$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. The structure module is quasi-coherent and generated by $1$, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. For $i:Z\hookrightarrow D$, [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] says that $\mathcal I_Z$ is a quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal O_D$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] now makes $\mathcal I_Z$ coherent. This proves the coherence required for vanishing without presupposing any vanishing or any finite generation of the ideal.

Here are also the local-ring assertions used in the statement. $D$ is a smooth connected curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves]: $k$ is algebraically closed, $D$ is of finite type and separated over $k$ because proper morphisms are separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], it has dimension one, and it is nonempty and connected because it is integral. At every $y\in T$, [lem-sc-smooth-regular] makes $R_y$ a regular local domain, hence Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-sc-point-cartier], the reduced point $y$ is locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor; at $y$ its ideal is $\mathfrak m_y$. Thus $\mathfrak m_y=(u_y)$ with $u_y\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]: every nonzero element of $R_y$ is $v u_y^r$ with $v$ a unit and $r\ge0$. If $v u_y^r=w u_y^s$ with $r<s$, cancellation in the domain gives $v=w u_y^{s-r}\in\mathfrak m_y$, contradicting that $v$ is a unit. The exponent is therefore unique. These are precisely the DVR properties spelled out in the item.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), condition (4) and final assertion; varieties.tex Tags 056S (lemma-smooth-regular) and 0B8Y (lemma-regular-point-on-curve).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] with $X=D$, $\mathcal L=A$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_D$. Its finite-type and quasi-coherence hypotheses were verified in step 1, and $A$ is ample and invertible by hypothesis. Since $\mathcal O_D\otimes A^{\otimes n}\cong A^{\otimes n}$ by multiplication, there is a bound $N_g$ for global generation for every $n\ge N_g$. If the theorem supplies an integer bound, replace it by its maximum with $0$.

source.place: Tag 01Q3 (proposition-characterize-ample), implication (1) to (7), with the structure module.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-serre-vanishing] with the Noetherian ring $k$, the proper structure morphism $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the coherent module $\mathcal I_Z$ from step 1, and the ample invertible module $A$. It gives $N_v\ge0$ for which $H^1(D,\mathcal I_Z\otimes A^{\otimes n})=0$ for every $n\ge N_v$. Set $n_0=\max\{1,N_g,N_v\}$. This one bound supplies global generation and the asserted vanishing simultaneously for every $n\ge n_0$. Fix such an $n$ and put $L=A^{\otimes n}$.

source.place: Tag 02O1 (lemma-kill-by-twisting), affine-base cohomology form, with p=1.

proof.text:
The ideal multiplication and restriction maps form
$0\to\mathcal I_Z\otimes L\to L\to i_*(L|_Z)\to0$.
Choose a frame of $A$ locally; its $n$-fold tensor is a frame $e$ of $L$. Here $L|_Z=i^*L$ is the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; since $i^*\mathcal O_D=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{i^{-1}\mathcal O_D}i^{-1}\mathcal O_D=\mathcal O_Z$, the restricted frame $1\otimes e$ is a frame of $L|_Z$ over the preimage of that open. In these coordinates the maps are the inclusion and quotient in
$0\to\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_D\to i_*\mathcal O_Z\to0$,
by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. At $y\in T$ this is $0\to\mathfrak m_y^2\to R_y\to R_y/\mathfrak m_y^2\to0$, which is exact. Outside $T$, a neighbourhood disjoint from $Z$ makes it $0\to\mathcal O_D\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_D\to0\to0$, also exact. On overlaps a change of frame multiplies all coefficients by the same transition unit, so these are the stated global maps. The stalk criterion [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] proves their exactness everywhere.

source.place: Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian), exactness on stalks; schemes.tex Tag 01HK (definition-closed-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces). Agent local-frame tensor calculation.

proof.text:
The long exact cohomology sequence supplied by [pqf-def-cohomology] for step 5 contains
$\Gamma(D,L)\longrightarrow\Gamma(D,i_*(L|_Z))\longrightarrow H^1(D,\mathcal I_Z\otimes L)$.
The last group is zero by step 4, so exactness says that the first arrow is onto. By the definition of direct image, $\Gamma(D,i_*(L|_Z))=\Gamma(Z,L|_Z)$, and that arrow is restriction, as is visible in the local frames of step 5. This is precisely the requested surjective map.

source.place: Tag 01DZ (section-cohomology-sheaves), the universal delta-functor on modules and its connecting sequence.

proof.text: The finite support $T$ is discrete as a subspace: each singleton is closed, and its complement is a finite union of closed singletons, hence is also closed. Thus $Z$ is covered by disjoint open singletons $Z_y$, $y\in T$. A sheaf on a singleton has global sections equal to its stalk. In particular the ring of $Z_y$ is $R_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$, and $L|_{Z_y}$ is free of rank one: a local frame exists because $L$ is locally free of rank one, and its open neighbourhood in $Z_y$ must be all of $Z_y$. For the specified frames $e_y$, choose the local section $(u\bmod\mathfrak m_x^2)e_x$ on $Z_x$ and $e_y$ on each $Z_y$ with $y\ne x$. These sections agree on their empty overlaps and hence glue by the sheaf axiom to $b\in\Gamma(Z,L|_Z)$. Step 6 gives a lift $a\in\Gamma(D,L)$, with exactly the prescribed coefficients.

source.place: Tag 006T (definition-sheaf), gluing on the disjoint open cover by the singleton components of Z; agent deduction from the given local rings.

proof.text:
To interpret the coefficients in $R_y$, start with any local frame of $L$ near $y$. The chosen frame $e_y$ on $Z_y$ differs from its restriction by a unit of $R_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$. A lift of that unit to $R_y$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_y$, so is a unit; multiplying the local frame by its germ and shrinking gives a frame lifting $e_y$. At $x$ the coefficient of $a$ is then $u+c u^2=u(1+cu)$ for some $c\in R_x$. Here $1+cu$ is a unit and $u
